decisions.title: GitHub write primitive: contract's non-forced ref PATCH versus R2's guarded GraphQL commit
decisions.statement: Owner-approved in docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-26.md (indy-init PR #20, OD-INDY-9). causa-storage v1.0.0 stays the wire contract. For GitHub, one semantic command is published as one GraphQL createCommitOnBranch carrying the events append, manifest and snapshot, with expectedHeadOid set to the commit the deciding state was read at. A refusal on a moved head is a non-fast-forward under section 9.4.2; success is reported only after a re-read at the new head (9.4.3). The non-forced REST ref update is not conforming. The exception holds until causa-storage 1.1.0 (STORAGE-003).
constraints: causa-storage v1.0.0 paths, file sets, schemas, fixtures and identities unchanged; sections 9.4.2 to 9.4.5 apply
One createCommitOnBranch per semantic command, with expectedHeadOid set to the commit the deciding state was read at; that commit is the provider version token
A refusal on a moved head is a non-fast-forward: reload, re-verify, rebase or report conflict, never force
Success only after a re-read at the new head; a failure after sending is unknown
No REST ref update for publication
alternatives: (a) Owner exception: causa-storage v1.0.0 wire format, paths and section 9.4.2-9.4.5 unchanged; the conforming GitHub publication mechanism of 9.4.1 is one GraphQL createCommitOnBranch carrying the three files, with expectedHeadOid set to the commit the decision was read at
(b) Version the contract (causa-storage 1.1.0, STORAGE-003) with the same rule; schemas and fixtures unchanged, new compatibility lock and release tag through causa-data's release workflow
(c) Keep the REST non-forced ref update (rejected: Rehearsal 2 review 6 proved it cannot compare-and-swap)
decisions.recommendation: (a) for Rehearsal 4 and the event; (b) after the event. (a) changes no data format, schema identity or fixture, needs no upstream release, and keeps optimistic concurrency (the decision's base commit stays the concurrency token, a moved head is refused and handled as a conflict). The exact amendment text is in readiness/CONTRACT-RESOLUTION.md.
consequences: CT-007 unblocks; T04 completes by recording the exception
DCT-001/DCT-003 and the T18 recordings target createCommitOnBranch and its refusal on a moved head

decisions.statement: Owner-approved in docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-26.md (indy-init PR #20, OD-INDY-11). The structured AI proposal loop and time travel / semantic diff (T27, T28) are excluded from Rehearsal 4. The proposal-authority invariant (D-004) and prompt/data boundaries (R11.4) stay in scope. The event's scope for these features is decided from the Rehearsal 4 result (R4 section 6). decisions.title: User authentication mechanism for the connect flow
decisions.statement: Owner-approved in docs/OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-26.md (indy-init PR #20, OD-INDY-10). Connect takes a fine-grained personal access token for the selected data repository only (Contents read/write, Metadata read, short expiry), held in memory only, re-entered after reload and sent only in the Authorization header. Classic tokens granting repo or admin scopes are refused. Every connection needs a credential; there is no anonymous mode. The CI live job uses the separate CAUSA_GITHUB_TOKEN secret.
constraints: Token scoped to the selected data repository: Contents read/write, Metadata read, short expiry
Held in memory only: never in localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, URLs, logs, error text, events or files; re-entered after reload
Sent only in the Authorization header
Classic tokens whose X-OAuth-Scopes grant repo or admin scopes are refused
A credential for every connection; no anonymous mode
Permission fields are advisory (DC-004)
Browser credentials and the CI secret CAUSA_GITHUB_TOKEN are separate
alternatives: (a) Fine-grained personal access token entered by the user in the Connect form: limited to the selected data repository (Contents read/write, Metadata read), short expiry, held in memory only (re-entered after reload, EXT-DATA-004), sent only in the Authorization header; the app reads X-OAuth-Scopes (exposed by api.github.com CORS) and refuses classic tokens carrying 'repo' or admin scopes

(b) GitHub App user token through the device flow: needs a token-exchange service, because a static page cannot call GitHub's login endpoints cross-origin (to be verified; this session's proxy prevented the check); adds a service outside static hosting
(c) OAuth web flow: needs a client secret and therefore a backend
decisions.recommendation: (a), with a credential required for every connection (no anonymous mode: Rehearsal 3 hit GitHub's exhausted anonymous quota). It needs no service, works in iPad Safari (plain fetch with an Authorization header; api.github.com answers Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *), and keeps least privilege. The CI live job uses the separate CAUSA_GITHUB_TOKEN Actions secret, never the browser path.
consequences: CT-017 becomes defined; DCT-004 covers absent permission fields
Connect UI: repository, branch, workspace, token field (type=password, autocomplete=off), clear refusal messages
PRE-AUTH-02 verifies the CI token is not a broad classic token
